results.title: Over 68% SIR enumeration forms digitised: ECI - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/national: ECI's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and electoral roll digitisation progress.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reported that over 68% of enumeration forms for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls have been digitised across 12 States and UTs.
notes.fact_box: The SIR is being conducted in 12 States/UTs including Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep. As of November 27, 2025, 34,86,60,338 forms (68% of existing electors) have been digitised.

prelims_pointers.text: 34,86,60,338 enumeration forms digitised as of November 27, 2025
Lakshadweep and Goa reported high digitisation rates of 99.9% and 89.77% respectively
Booth-level officers (BLOs) are responsible for collecting forms and uploading data to the ECI website
The enumeration phase is scheduled to run from November 4 to December 4

notes.mains_question: Discuss the significance of digitising electoral rolls in ensuring the integrity of the democratic process and reducing electoral fraud in India.
mains_dimensions: Data integrity: Real-time digitisation by BLOs reduces manual entry errors and prevents duplicate entries
Inclusion gap: Disparity in digitisation rates between states like Lakshadweep and Uttar Pradesh highlights uneven infrastructure
Transparency: Publicly accessible draft lists and online objection filing mechanisms enhance voter trust
